record.context_brief: classification of complemented subspaces of L1
record.original_question: Is every infinite-dimensional complemented subspace of L1[0,1] isomorphic either to L1[0,1] itself or to ℓ1? Equivalently, is every infinite-dimensional complemented subspace of L1[0,1] isomorphic to some L1(ν)-space?

evidence.quote: Problem 5. ([79]) Is every (infinite dimensional) complemented subspace of L1 isomorphic to either L1 or `1 (equivalently, to an L1(ν)-space)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L_1[0,1]$ denote the Banach space of (equivalence classes of) Lebesgue-integrable real-valued functions on $[0,1]$ with norm $\|f\|_1=\int_0^1|f(t)|\,dt$, and let $\ell_1$ denote the Banach space of absolutely summable real sequences. A closed subspace $X$ of a Banach space $Y$ is said to be complemented in $Y$ if there exists a bounded linear projection $P:Y	o Y$ with range $X$. Two Banach spaces are isomorphic if there is a bounded linear bijection between them with bounded inverse. For a positive (possibly non-$\sigma$-finite) measure $
u$ on a measurable space, $L_1(
u)$ denotes the corresponding Lebesgue space of integrable functions.

Question: Is every infinite-dimensional complemented subspace of $L_1[0,1]$ isomorphic either to $L_1[0,1]$ or to $\ell_1$? Equivalently, is every infinite-dimensional complemented subspace of $L_1[0,1]$ isomorphic to $L_1(
u)$ for some measure $
u$?
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of complemented subspaces of $L_1[0,1]$ is a long-standing open problem in Banach space theory. The analogous problem for $C(K)$-spaces was recently resolved negatively by Plebanek and Salguero-Alarcón (2023), but the $L_1$ version remains unsolved as of 2025, as confirmed by recent surveys including the 2025 paper on complemented subspaces of Banach lattices by de Hevia and Tradacete.

status_evidence.title: Complemented subspaces of Banach lattices (de Hevia, Tradacete)
status_evidence.snippet: Problem P2 (the L1 case) is still open, while Problem P1 (for C(K)-spaces) has recently been answered in the negative by Plebanek and Salguero-Alarcón.
status_evidence.claim: The complemented subspace problem for L1 remains open as of 2025.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on the Complemented Subspace Problem
status_evidence.snippet: It is conjectured that every complemented subspace of L1[0,1] is isomorphic to ℓ1 or to L1[0,1].
status_evidence.claim: This is a classical conjecture, still open.
